title: 5 Days in Milwaukee
subtitle: Fencing Summer Nationals, a Chicago day trip & the Historic Third Ward
summary: Five days in Milwaukee for USA Fencing Summer Nationals: Josh competing at the Baird Center, a RiverWalk and Third Ward stroll, a day trip to Chicago on the Hiawatha, a Lakefront Brewery tour, and brunch at the Pfister.

glance.label: Base
glance.value: The Trade, Autograph Collection, downtown Milwaukee (4 nights)

glance.label: Why we're here
glance.value: USA Fencing Summer Nationals at the Baird Center – Josh fencing Division 2 and Division 1A Men's Épée

glance.label: Day trip
glance.value: Chicago by Amtrak Hiawatha – Millennium Park, the Riverwalk, Navy Pier and the Centennial Wheel

glance.label: Getting around
glance.value: Mostly on foot downtown, Uber when short on time, and the free Hop streetcar between neighborhoods

glance.label: Highlights
glance.value: Lakefront Brewery tour, Purple Door Ice Cream, brunch at the Pfister, a day in Chicago

intro: Josh's Summer Nationals meant a week built around two fencing days at the Baird Center, with everything else fit around them: a landing day downtown, a full day trip to Chicago, and a couple of easier mornings before his later bout on the last day. The Trade put us a short walk from the convention center, the RiverWalk and the Third Ward, so we barely needed the car-free city's transit beyond The Hop streetcar.

We kept fencing days simple – coffee and snacks instead of a sit-down breakfast, home base close enough to shower and regroup between rounds – and used the lighter days for the RiverWalk, Lakefront Brewery, brunch at the Pfister and a full day across the border in Chicago on the Hiawatha.

days_plan.label: Day 1
days_plan.title: Landing day – the Baird Center, the RiverWalk & the Third Ward
days_plan.text: A morning flight in, a quick stop at the fencing venue to cheer on a friend and get Josh's gear checked, then an afternoon easing into downtown Milwaukee on foot before our first dinner reservation.

items.text: Fly United flight UA3554 from Newark (EWR), landing in Milwaukee (MKE) at 10:57 AM
Uber to The Trade, Autograph Collection to check in or at least hold our luggage
Walk to the Baird Center to catch Lottie fencing 70+ Vet Women's Épée, if we make it in time, and have Josh do his equipment check
Lunch – walk and see what's on the way; Craft at the hotel is the fallback if we're hungry and nothing else stands out, though it's pricier with fewer casual options
Back to the hotel to drop off fencing gear, freshen up and get properly checked in

Walk the Milwaukee RiverWalk into the Historic Third Ward – a scenic 3-mile river path with public art and bridges, then cobblestone streets, galleries and boutiques just a few minutes further on foot
Lakeshore State Park for the pebbly shoreline, prairie landscaping and the fishing pier where it links up with the Oak Leaf and Hank Aaron trails
Dinner at The Social American Tavern, 611 N Broadway (OpenTable reservation)

days_plan.tip: Quick water and snack stops downtown: Tourist Convenience at 240 W Wells St, right between the hotel blocks; The Grand Convenient about 0.3 miles away; or the Walgreens at 275 W Wisconsin Ave, about a 5-minute walk.

days_plan.label: Day 2
days_plan.title: A day trip to Chicago on the Hiawatha
days_plan.text: The Amtrak Hiawatha makes Chicago an easy day trip from Milwaukee: Millennium Park and The Bean, a walk along the Riverwalk, deep dish or lobster rolls for lunch, and an afternoon at Navy Pier before the train back for a lighter dinner at the hotel.

items.text: Leave the hotel and walk to the Milwaukee Intermodal Station
Depart Milwaukee on the Amtrak Hiawatha
Arrive at Union Station, Chicago
Millennium Park & The Bean – Cloud Gate, Crown Fountain and Lurie Garden, with skyline views and photos
Walk the Chicago Riverwalk east toward the lake – bridges, architecture and people-watching, with a cold drink stop at Tiny Tapp or Island Party Hut
Lunch – Giordano's deep dish at 730 N Rush St (call ahead around 11:30 AM to have it ready by noon) or Luke's Lobster at 134 N LaSalle St for a faster lobster or crab roll
Walk or Uber to Navy Pier, 600 E Grand Ave, for lake views, shops and a lemonade or ice cream
Ride the Centennial Wheel – about 15 minutes with skyline and lake views
Coffee or a donut break – Do-Rite Donuts or the Offshore Café on the pier, if we want one
Walk or Uber back to Union Station, aiming to be there by 4:45 PM
Return train to Milwaukee on the Hiawatha
Walk back toward the hotel, keeping an eye out for a better dinner option along the way
Dinner reservation at Craft, the hotel restaurant (OpenTable) – nothing too heavy, since Josh fences tomorrow

days_plan.tip: Other quick lunch options near the Riverwalk: Brown Bag Seafood Co. at 340 E Randolph St for seafood bowls and tacos, America's Dog & Burger inside Navy Pier for classic Chicago dogs, Small Cheval near River North for quick-serve burgers, or Big City Chicken inside Navy Pier for fried chicken sandwiches. Bring comfortable shoes, sun protection, a refillable water bottle and a light layer for the lake breeze.

days_plan.label: Day 3
days_plan.title: Josh's Division 2 Men's Épée, Lakefront Brewery & Lake Park
days_plan.text: Josh's first fencing day at the Baird Center, then an afternoon at Lakefront Brewery for the tour and the cheese curds, a walk through Lake Park toward Juneau Park, and ice cream before an early night.

items.text: Coffee and a bite from the hotel lobby, or bars and snacks brought along for breakfast
Leave the hotel and walk to the Baird Center, 400 W Wisconsin Ave
Josh's Division 2 Men's Épée tournament at the Baird Center
Back to the hotel after fencing for Josh to shower
Walk to Lakefront Brewery
Lakefront Brewery Tour, 1872 N Commerce St – Uber instead if we're short on time
After the tour, grab a table for lunch if one's free – the cheese curds are supposed to be excellent
Walk to Lake Park, explore, and walk south toward Juneau Park
Purple Door Ice Cream, 205 S 2nd St (open until 10 PM) – good reviews and unique flavors
Head back toward the hotel and get ready for tomorrow

days_plan.tip: Lakefront Brewery's tours run on a schedule and the on-site restaurant fills up fast right after – grab a table as soon as the tour ends if lunch there is the plan.

days_plan.label: Day 4
days_plan.title: A slow morning, brunch at the Pfister & Division 1A
days_plan.text: A late start, brunch at the Pfister before the lunch menu takes over, Josh's second fencing day in the afternoon, and a low-key dinner around the corner from the hotel once we're packed for tomorrow's early flight.

items.text: Sleep in
Walk to brunch at Cafe at the Pfister, 424 E Wisconsin Ave – breakfast is only served until 11 AM, when the lunch menu takes over; no reservation, so we can detour if another spot catches our eye
Leave the hotel and walk to the Baird Center
Josh's Division 1A Men's Épée tournament at the Baird Center
Back to the hotel after fencing for Josh to shower, and start packing – a very early departure tomorrow
Dinner at Oak Barrel Public House, around the corner from the hotel (reviews are mixed, but it's convenient on a packing night)

days_plan.tip: Café at the Pfister stops serving breakfast at 11 AM sharp – go early if the morning menu is the point.

days_plan.label: Day 5
days_plan.title: Early flight home
days_plan.text: A 6 AM flight means leaving the hotel in the dark, but we're back in Newark by mid-morning.

stays.name: The Trade, Autograph Collection
stays.note: Walking distance to the Baird Center, the RiverWalk and the Third Ward; Craft, the hotel restaurant, is a convenient but pricier fallback.

eats.name: The Social American Tavern
eats.note: Our first-night dinner, booked on OpenTable.

eats.name: Craft
eats.note: The hotel restaurant – reliable and no-Uber-needed, but on the pricier side with fewer casual options. Good for a lighter dinner before a fencing day.

eats.name: Giordano's
eats.note: Famous Chicago-style deep dish – takes about 45 minutes to bake, so call ahead (312-951-0747) and ask for it ready by noon.

eats.name: Luke's Lobster
eats.note: Fast-casual lobster, crab and shrimp rolls – ask for no mayo. About $18 for a roll; quick enough to eat at the Riverwalk.

eats.name: Lakefront Brewery
eats.note: Tour the brewery, then stay for lunch if a table's free – the cheese curds are supposed to be excellent.

eats.name: Purple Door Ice Cream
eats.note: Open until 10 PM, with good reviews and unique flavors.

eats.name: Cafe at the Pfister
eats.note: Breakfast only served until 11 AM, then the lunch menu starts. No reservation needed.

eats.name: Oak Barrel Public House
eats.place: Around the corner from The Trade
eats.note: Convenient on a packing night; reviews are mixed.

eats.name: Milwaukee Public Market
eats.note: A good casual lunch stop if there's time on either end of the trip.

book_ahead: United Airlines flights to and from MKE
Amtrak Hiawatha tickets to Chicago and back
Centennial Wheel tickets at Navy Pier
Dinner at The Social American Tavern (OpenTable)
Call Giordano's ahead to time a deep-dish pickup

tips.title: The Hop streetcar is free
tips.text: No tickets or vouchers needed – just hop on and off at any stop along the downtown route. It runs every 10–20 minutes (Mon–Fri 5 AM–12 AM, shorter hours on weekends) and connects Milwaukee Intermodal, the Third Ward, East Town, the Lower East Side and downtown – handy for stretches between the RiverWalk, Third Ward or lakeshore areas that we don't feel like walking.

tips.title: Pace fencing days around the schedule, not the clock
tips.text: Grab-and-go coffee and snacks instead of a sit-down breakfast, and keep the hotel close enough to shower and regroup between rounds. The Baird Center is a short walk from The Trade, which made both tournament days easier.

tips.title: If there's extra time
tips.text: The Pabst Mansion and the Milwaukee Art Museum are both worth a visit if the schedule allows, and the Milwaukee Public Market in the Third Ward is a good casual lunch stop.
